content: chicos, si quieren tiktoks más tranquilos sobre la vida tranquila en su fyp,,asegúrense de escribir un comentario largo como este o copiar y pegar. No sé por qué, pero últimamente he estado locamente obsesionado con con la vida tranquila y medida. Como mañanas tranquilas, una cama hecha, ventanas abiertas para respirar aire fresco, estudiar música suave, llevar un diario, cuidarse, limpiar la habitación, beber agua y simplemente una vida suave y tranquila. Hay algo muy relajante en ello: en rutinas tranquilas y en aprender a disfrutar de momentos sencillos. Me encantan los videos en los que la gente lee libros, cocina con calma, limpia sus habitaciones, sale con auriculares, mira atardeceres, va a bibliotecas, usa ropa acogedora, cuida las plantas y se sienta con una luz natural suave. Todo esto es tan curativo y refrescante que ni siquiera puedo explicar. Y también tengo una hiperfijación en habitaciones minimalistas y acogedoras, colores neutros cálidos, listas de reproducción tranquilas, cafés tranquilos, estudios nocturnos, amistades tranquilas, pequeños hábitos diarios y, en general, estilos de vida suaves y relajantes que hacen que todo sea más lento, limpio y significativo Copien y peguen

Qingshan Green Lake: stroll along the lake and enjoy the serene greenery 🍃 5. 72 Wonder Tower: party with locals and see the city lights from above ✨ 6. Longjing Tea Fields: sip fresh tea in the lush plantations 🍵 7. Great Wall of China: slide down sections of this iconic wonder 🧱 8. Fenghuang Ancient Village: get lost in winding streets and riverside scenery 🏘️ 9. Hong’en Temple at night: see the temple beautifully illuminated after dark 🕯️ 10. Chinese food: try everything from spicy hotpot to dumplings and street snacks 🍜 11. Chengdu: meet the giant pandas and learn about conservation 🐼 12. The Bund, Shanghai: stroll along the riverside at night and admire the skyline 🌃 13. Leifeng Pagoda: climb this historic pagoda and take in views of West Lake 🕍 14. Liziba Station: watch the famous train pass through a building 🚆 15. Glass Bridge: walk across the Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge 🌉 16. Beijing Roast Duck: taste this iconic dish in the city where it all began 🦆 17. West Lake, Hangzhou: relax by the water, rent a boat, or enjoy a sunset stroll 🌅 18. Get lost in random streets: sometimes the best discoveries are off the beaten path 🚶‍♂️ 19. People’s Park: dance or join locals for morning exercises 💃 20. Qingshan Green Lake: stroll along the lake and enjoy the serene greenery 🍃 5. 72 Wonder Tower: party with locals and see the city lights from above ✨ 6. Longjing Tea Fields: sip fresh tea in the lush plantations 🍵 7. Great Wall of China: slide down sections of this iconic wonder 🧱 8. Fenghuang Ancient Village: get lost in winding streets and riverside scenery 🏘️ 9. Hong’en Temple at night: see the temple beautifully illuminated after dark 🕯️ 10. Chinese food: try everything from spicy hotpot to dumplings and street snacks 🍜 11. Chengdu: meet the giant pandas and learn about conservation 🐼 12. The Bund, Shanghai: stroll along the riverside at night and admire the skyline 🌃 13. Leifeng Pagoda: climb this historic pagoda and take in views of West Lake 🕍 14. Liziba Station: watch the famous train pass through a building 🚆 15. Glass Bridge: walk across the Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge 🌉 16. Beijing Roast Duck: taste this iconic dish in the city where it all began 🦆 17. West Lake, Hangzhou: relax by the water, rent a boat, or enjoy a sunset stroll 🌅 18. content: Gente, se vocês querem mais TikToks de estilo de vida calmo e tranquilo no fyp, escrevam um comentário longo como esse ou copiem e colem. Não sei por quê, mas eu tenho estado tão obcecada por uma vida lenta e tranquila ultimamente. Tipo manhãs silenciosas, arrumar a cama, abrir as janelas pra entrar ar fresco, estudar com música de fundo suave, escrever num diário, cuidar de si mesma, limpar o quarto, beber água e simplesmente viver com gentileza. Tem algo muito aconchegante em rotinas calmas e aprender a aproveitar momentos simples. Eu amo vídeos de pessoas lendo livros, cozinhando em paz, organizando o espaço, andando na rua de fone de ouvido, pôr do sol, bibliotecas, looks aconchegantes, plantas e uma luz natural suave. Tudo isso parece tão curador e revigorante de um jeito que eu nem sei explicar. E também eu tenho uma hiperfixação em quartos minimalistas e aconchegantes, cores neutras e quentes, playlists calmas, cafés tranquilos, estudar de madrugada, amizades silenciosas, pequenos hábitos do dia a dia e, no geral, estilos de vida suaves e confortantes que fazem tudo parecer mais devagar, mais limpo e mais significativo.

content: Any insight or advice on language barriers? I never want to assume that that most places will be able to accommodate English speakers, but I also don’t want to assume I’d be able to learn enough of any Chinese language that I could communicate properly! Especially because I assume many of these places have different languages or dialects because a trip like this covers a lot of ground (and this is only an educated assumption because I don’t specifically know much about specific regions and language in China). I love learning languages, but I know I’ll never be able to learn every language in the world despite any desire to lol. I can stumble through a lot of Western Europe using a remedial understanding of a couple European languages and my native English, but outside of Europe I have no formal language education or experience, but I’d still like to explore the world.

content: 江西上饒靈山（靈應山）是國家4A級旅遊景區與國家級風景名勝區，以奇峰怪石（72奇峰）、道教「天下第三十三福地」及獨特花崗岩環狀山體地貌著稱。主峰海拔1,496米，有「睡美人」之美譽，景區設有高空棧道、雲端懸崖玻璃棧道、天空之鏡及超長登山電梯，適宜休閒觀光與攝影。
video_caption: 靈山擁有亞洲最長室外登山扶梯，且耗資1.3億打造的超級電梯，55分鐘直達山頂，老人小孩都能輕鬆征服雲海奇峰！ 電梯全長753.2米，10段扶梯，垂直高度267米，相當於88層樓 #旅行 #旅遊 #江西 #jiangxi #chinatravel

content: Chicos, si quieren tiktoks más tranquilos sobre la vida tranquila en su fyp,,asegúrense de escribir un comentario largo como este o copiar y pegar. No sé por qué, pero últimamente he estado locamente obsesionado con con la vida tranquila y medida. Como mañanas tranquilas, una cama hecha, ventanas abiertas para respirar aire fresco, estudiar música suave, llevar un diario, cuidarse, limpiar la habitación, beber agua y simplemente una vida suave y tranquila. Hay algo muy relajante en ello: en rutinas tranquilas y en aprender a disfrutar de momentos sencillos. Me encantan los videos en los que la gente lee libros, cocina con calma, limpia sus habitaciones, sale con auriculares, mira atardeceres, va a bibliotecas, usa ropa acogedora, cuida las plantas y se sienta con una luz natural suave. Todo esto es tan curativo y refrescante que ni siquiera puedo explicar. Y también tengo una hiperfijación en habitaciones minimalistas y acogedoras, colores neutros cálidos, listas de reproducción tranquilas, cafés tranquilos, estudios nocturnos, amistades tranquilas, pequeños hábitos diarios y, en general, estilos de vida suaves y relajantes que hacen que todo sea más lento, limpio y significativo Copie y pegue sonion 😂✌️🥀🗣️🔥

Fenghuang Ancient Village: get lost in winding streets and riverside scenery 🏘️ 9. Hong’en Temple at night: see the temple beautifully illuminated after dark 🕯️ 10. Chinese food: try everything from spicy hotpot to dumplings and street snacks 🍜 11. Chengdu: meet the giant pandas and learn about conservation 🐼 12. The Bund, Shanghai: stroll along the riverside at night and admire the skyline 🌃 13. Leifeng Pagoda: climb this historic pagoda and take in views of West Lake 🕍 14. Liziba Station: watch the famous train pass through a building 🚆 15. Glass Bridge: walk across the Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge 🌉 16. Beijing Roast Duck: taste this iconic dish in the city where it all began 🦆 17. West Lake, Hangzhou: relax by the water, rent a boat, or enjoy a sunset stroll 🌅 18. content: Chinese people also make an effort to learn the local language or use translation apps when they travel or live abroad. Likewise, when foreigners visit China, they shouldn’t complain that local people don’t speak English. Instead, they can try communicating in Chinese or use a translation app to bridge the language gap. People in China are not obligated to speak English, so it’s best not to assume that everyone should. It’s also unfair to laugh at or look down on someone because they don’t speak English. They are simply using their own language in their own country, where they live their daily lives. That said, many public places and popular tourist attractions in China do provide English services, English signs, and tourist assistance. More importantly, many Chinese people are willing to help visitors with kindness, even if they don’t speak fluent English. With a little patience and mutual effort, communication is usually not a problem.

The art of Chinese silk flower making, known as ronghua (velvet flower), is an ancient craft that combines exquisite precision with poetic beauty, dating back over 1,700 years. Flourishing during the Tang Dynasty (618–907), where it adorned the hair of court ladies, it later became a beloved accessory for weddings and festivals, as its name is a homophone for "glory" and a symbol of prosperity. The creation process is painstaking and can involve over a hundred individual steps. It begins with preparing raw silk, which is dyed in vibrant hues, stretched taut over wooden frames, and then carefully cut into petal shapes. Each petal, unique in form and size, is then shaped entirely by hand using heated tools to curl, crease, and give it a lifelike three-dimensional volume. These delicate components are finally assembled around a metal wire stem, layered and twisted to mimic nature’s own designs, resulting in blossoms so realistic they seem to capture a fleeting moment of spring. Today, this heritage craft is experiencing a remarkable revival, led by master artisans like Zhao Shuxian, a living national treasure, who has collaborated with luxury brands such as Dior and LVMH to bring ronghua to international runways. Bridging ancient tradition with contemporary fashion, these ethereal silk flowers continue to bloom, transitioning gracefully from the palaces of emperors to the global stage of haute couture. #capcut #duet #foryoupage #foryou #fyp @maoshifu-food @Med Human

No sé por qué, pero últimamente he estado obsesionada con vivir en paz y con calma. Como mañanas silenciosas, tender tu cama, abrir las ventanas para tomar aire fresco, estudiar con música suave, escribir en tu diario, cuidarte, limpiar tu cuarto, tomar agua y simplemente vivir con suavidad. Hay algo muy reconfortante en las rutinas tranquilas y aprender a disfrutar los momentos simples. Amo los videos de gente leyendo libros, cocinando en paz, organizando su espacio, caminando afuera con audífonos, atardeceres, bibliotecas, outfits acogedores, plantas y una luz natural suave. Todo se siente tan sanador y refrescante de una forma que no puedo explicar. Y también tengo una hiperfijación en cuartos minimalistas y acogedores, colores neutros cálidos, playlists tranquilas, cafés en paz, estudiar de noche, amistades silenciosas, pequeños hábitos diarios y, en general, estilos de vida suaves y reconfortantes que hacen que todo se sienta más lento, más limpio y más significativo.

content: This show is set during China’s Tang dynasty, an influential Chinese golden age known for its openness and Silk Road trade. Back then many Arab merchants traveled across the Silk Road with camel caravans to the Tang Empire for trade. They also introduced Islam to China, and brought back technologies such as papermaking and gunpowder and spread them westward through these trade networks. This kind of cultural exchange was beautiful, bringing together people from different civilizations and enriching both cultures.

The art of Chinese silk flower making, known as ronghua (velvet flower), is an ancient craft that combines exquisite precision with poetic beauty, dating back over 1,700 years. Flourishing during the Tang Dynasty (618–907), where it adorned the hair of court ladies, it later became a beloved accessory for weddings and festivals, as its name is a homophone for "glory" and a symbol of prosperity. The creation process is painstaking and can involve over a hundred individual steps. It begins with preparing raw silk, which is dyed in vibrant hues, stretched taut over wooden frames, and then carefully cut into petal shapes. Each petal, unique in form and size, is then shaped entirely by hand using heated tools to curl, crease, and give it a lifelike three-dimensional volume. These delicate components are finally assembled around a metal wire stem, layered and twisted to mimic nature’s own designs, resulting in blossoms so realistic they seem to capture a fleeting moment of spring. Today, this heritage craft is experiencing a remarkable revival, led by master artisans like Zhao Shuxian, a living national treasure, who has collaborated with luxury brands such as Dior and LVMH to bring ronghua to international runways. Bridging ancient tradition with contemporary fashion, these ethereal silk flowers continue to bloom, transitioning gracefully from the palaces of emperors to the global stage of haute couture. #capcut #duet #foryoupage #foryou #fyp @maoshifu-food @Med Human

content: @qefw:Японская эстетика — это не просто набор правил о прекрасном, а фундаментальное мировоззрение, сформированное синтоизмом (одухотворение природы) и дзен-буддизмом (поиск истины в интуитивном прозрении). В её центре лежит принятие несовершенства и быстротечности мира. Ключевой принцип — Ваби-саби: умение находить красоту в простом, ветхом и недолговечном. Это очарование старого камня, покрытого мхом, или трещины на керамической чаше, которую не скрывают, а подчёркивают золотом (кинцуги). Дополняет его Югэн — красота намёка и недосказанности, когда смысл скрыт за пеленой тумана, и зрителю остаётся лишь догадываться о нём. Чувство Моно-но аварэ — это светлая печаль от осознания мимолётности вещей, острее всего переживаемая при любовании цветущей сакурой. Эти идеи пронизывают все виды искусства. В архитектуре и дизайне царит минимализм, пустота и функциональность (сибуй). Японский сад — это не клумба, а пейзаж для созерцания, где камни и вода значат больше, чем яркие краски. В поэзии хайку (всего три строки) главное — передать мгновение и дать простор воображению читателя. В чайной церемонии канон Ваби-саби достигает апогея в простоте утвари и тишине ритуала. Даже сегодня, от графического дизайна до архитектуры Тадао Андо, японская эстетика продолжает учить мир видеть душу в тишине, пустоте и несовершенстве, утверждая, что истинная красота не терпит суеты и скрыта в самом течении жизни.

The art of Chinese silk flower making, known as ronghua (velvet flower), is an ancient craft that combines exquisite precision with poetic beauty, dating back over 1,700 years. Flourishing during the Tang Dynasty (618–907), where it adorned the hair of court ladies, it later became a beloved accessory for weddings and festivals, as its name is a homophone for "glory" and a symbol of prosperity. The creation process is painstaking and can involve over a hundred individual steps. It begins with preparing raw silk, which is dyed in vibrant hues, stretched taut over wooden frames, and then carefully cut into petal shapes. Each petal, unique in form and size, is then shaped entirely by hand using heated tools to curl, crease, and give it a lifelike three-dimensional volume. These delicate components are finally assembled around a metal wire stem, layered and twisted to mimic nature’s own designs, resulting in blossoms so realistic they seem to capture a fleeting moment of spring. Today, this heritage craft is experiencing a remarkable revival, led by master artisans like Zhao Shuxian, a living national treasure, who has collaborated with luxury brands such as Dior and LVMH to bring ronghua to international runways. Bridging ancient tradition with contemporary fashion, these ethereal silk flowers continue to bloom, transitioning gracefully from the palaces of emperors to the global stage of haute couture. #capcut #duet #foryoupage #foryou #fyp @maoshifu-food @Med Human

video_caption: Spending over a month to create, with velvet flowers, a beautiful memory that belongs uniquely to summer. making fascinating silk flowers 🌺🌹. rural life in China countryside life and cooking Chinese craftswomen daily life vlog Chinese culture Chinese heritage Chinese food Chinese village Chinese craft Chinese lifestyle explore China visit China.  The art of Chinese silk flower making, known as ronghua (velvet flower), is an ancient craft that combines exquisite precision with poetic beauty, dating back over 1,700 years. Flourishing during the Tang Dynasty (618–907), where it adorned the hair of court ladies, it later became a beloved accessory for weddings and festivals, as its name is a homophone for "glory" and a symbol of prosperity. The creation process is painstaking and can involve over a hundred individual steps. It begins with preparing raw silk, which is dyed in vibrant hues, stretched taut over wooden frames, and then carefully cut into petal shapes. Each petal, unique in form and size, is then shaped entirely by hand using heated tools to curl, crease, and give it a lifelike three-dimensional volume. These delicate components are finally assembled around a metal wire stem, layered and twisted to mimic nature’s own designs, resulting in blossoms so realistic they seem to capture a fleeting moment of spring. Today, this heritage craft is experiencing a remarkable revival, led by master artisans like Zhao Shuxian, a living national treasure, who has collaborated with luxury brands such as Dior and LVMH to bring ronghua to international runways. Bridging ancient tradition with contemporary fashion, these ethereal silk flowers continue to bloom, transitioning gracefully from the palaces of emperors to the global stage of haute couture. #capcut #duet #foryoupage #foryou #fyp @maoshifu-food @Med Human
